children: The U.S. government is set to intervene in Elon Musk’s legal challenge against the European Union’s €120M ($136.5M) fine on X, adding Washington to the dispute over the bloc’s digital regulations.

The U.S. Department of Justice filed the request with the EU’s General Court supporting separate challenges by X and Musk seeking to overturn the European Commission’s December 2025 decision. The Commission imposed the fine jointly and severally on X and Musk for violations of the Digital Services Act.

“The European Commission inappropriately attempted to expand its regulatory authority to reach American companies not present or operating within its jurisdiction,” Assistant Attorney General Brett Shumate said.

The Commission said the fine followed a two-year investigation into X’s blue-check verification system, advertising repository, and access to public data for researchers. It was the first non-compliance decision under the DSA. The U.S. request does not itself overturn the fine. The General Court will decide whether Washington can participate in the proceedings.

title: U.S. backs Elon Musk’s challenge to EU’s €120M fine on X
